TimePeriod: Patriarchal era onward, c. 2000 BC and after
Region: The desert east of Egypt, from Havilah to Shur, and later the northern Arabian desert
History: The Ishmaelites descended from Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar (Genesis 16; 21). Genesis 25:12-18 lists his twelve sons, princes of their tribes, dwelling from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt. An Ishmaelite caravan carrying spices to Egypt bought Joseph from his brothers (Genesis 37:25-28; the same passage also calls the traders Midianites, and the two names are used together there). Gideon asked for the gold earrings of the Ishmaelite traders after defeating Midian (Judges 8:24), and Psalm 83:6 counts the Ishmaelites among the confederates against Israel.
Culture: Nomadic desert traders, living in tents and moving goods between Arabia and Egypt. Ishmael himself 'grew, and dwelt in the wilderness, and became an archer' (Genesis 21:20).
Religion: The text ties Ishmael's line to Abraham's God through Hagar's encounter at the well (Genesis 16) and God's promise to make Ishmael a great nation (Genesis 17:20), but it describes no distinct Ishmaelite religion.
BibleConnection: Ishmaelites carry Joseph into Egypt, setting the exodus story in motion, and stand as the desert kin of Israel: Abraham's other son's line, blessed yet outside the covenant promise.
KeyScriptures: Genesis 16:11-12; Genesis 21:20-21; Genesis 25:12-18; Genesis 37:25-28; Judges 8:24; Psalm 83:6
RelatedPeople: Abraham; Hagar; Ishmael; Isaac; Jacob; Joseph, Son of Jacob
RelatedEvents: Joseph and His Brothers; Hagar and Ishmael
